positioning: A B2B industrial vision brand focused on machine vision products and inspection applications. This is a portfolio concept, not a real company claim.
audience: Manufacturers, automation integrators, equipment builders and technical decision-makers.
promise: Make industrial vision clearer, more reliable and easier to apply.
logo_structure: Current website header artwork: graphic symbol at left, DEF Company wordmark and tagline at right. Treat this as the current horizontal lockup until the original editable logo artwork is reviewed.
logo_dos: Use the approved artwork on a background with sufficient contrast.
Keep clear space around the complete logo lockup.
Use the symbol alone only after confirming the symbol file is approved for standalone use.
logo_donts: Do not stretch, squeeze, skew or rotate the logo.
Do not recolor the logo or add shadows, outlines or gradients.
Do not rearrange the symbol, wordmark and tagline without an approved variant.
Do not place the logo over a busy image that reduces legibility.

typography_family: Inter (working proposal; confirm availability and licensing before finalizing)

type_styles.name: H1
type_styles.usage: Main headline on a page or large campaign visual.

type_styles.name: Body
type_styles.sample: Clear technical information for industrial decision-makers.

imagery_categories.name: Product Photography
imagery_categories.description: Clear product presentation with the camera or device as the main subject.
imagery_categories.use: Product pages, product one-pagers and product-led Stories.
imagery_categories.rules: Show the real product shape, ports, lens mount and key details accurately. Prefer clean backgrounds and controlled lighting.
imagery_categories.avoid: Distorted perspective, inaccurate retouching, cluttered backgrounds or cropped-away product features.

imagery_categories.name: Application Photography
imagery_categories.description: Show the camera or vision system working in a real industrial process.
imagery_categories.use: Industry Stories, solution explanations and exhibition graphics.
imagery_categories.rules: Make the inspection task and production context understandable. Keep the camera, inspected object or process visible where possible.
imagery_categories.avoid: Generic factory stock photos with no clear connection to the application.

imagery_categories.name: Technical Detail Images
imagery_categories.description: Close-ups, image samples, diagrams or annotated details that explain a technical capability.
imagery_categories.use: Technical articles, product pages and sales materials.
imagery_categories.rules: Prioritize accuracy, legibility and clear annotations. Verify technical labels with product information.
imagery_categories.avoid: Decorative overlays that obscure the technical subject or imply unverified performance.

imagery_categories.name: Brand & Event Photography
imagery_categories.description: Exhibition booths, demonstrations, team interactions and event environments.
imagery_categories.use: Trade Show pages, event recaps and social campaigns.
imagery_categories.rules: Show the booth, products and real interactions. Use purposeful framing and readable signage.
imagery_categories.avoid: Unclear event photos, accidental close-ups, low-resolution images or unrelated crowd scenes.

icon_style: Simple, consistent line icons with a shared stroke weight and restrained detail. Use icons to clarify technical concepts, not as decoration.
graphic_elements: Use restrained grids, thin technical lines, simple geometric blocks and clear data callouts. Avoid random futuristic effects, excessive gradients and decorative shapes that compete with product information.
grid_spacing: Use consistent alignment and a repeatable spacing scale. In Figma, start with 8 / 16 / 24 / 32 px spacing and use Auto Layout for repeatable groups. Adjust only when the format requires it.

layout_patterns.name: Image Left · Text Right
layout_patterns.description: A balanced two-column composition with a visual on the left and explanatory content on the right.
layout_patterns.structure: Image 40–50% / text 50–60%, aligned to a shared top edge.
layout_patterns.use: Product features, application explanations and website sections.
layout_patterns.figma: Create a horizontal Auto Layout frame; set image and text columns, align top, define a consistent gap and test responsive stacking.

layout_patterns.name: Image Top · Text Below
layout_patterns.description: A vertical card pattern with image first, then title and supporting copy.
layout_patterns.structure: Full-width image, title, short description and optional link.
layout_patterns.use: Story cards, Trade Show cards and social content previews.
layout_patterns.figma: Create a vertical Auto Layout frame; keep image ratio consistent and use shared text styles.

layout_patterns.name: Headline Top · Product Visual Below
layout_patterns.description: A strong headline above a dominant product or application visual.
layout_patterns.structure: Headline and short proof point above a large image.
layout_patterns.use: Trade show roll-up banners and campaign key visuals.
layout_patterns.figma: Use a vertical frame; establish headline hierarchy first, then allocate the largest visual area to the product or application.

layout_patterns.name: Split Panel
layout_patterns.description: A clean split between a colored information panel and a product or application image.
layout_patterns.use: Product one-pagers, presentation covers and exhibition graphics.
layout_patterns.figma: Use a two-column frame with a clear dividing edge, consistent margins and controlled accent color.

voice_attributes: Professional, precise, clear and helpful. Explain technical value without exaggerated claims.
writing_principles: Lead with the customer problem or application. Use specific technical language where verified. Keep claims measurable and supportable. Avoid vague superlatives and unsupported performance promises.
terminology: Use consistent product names and technical terms across the website, social content, exhibition materials and sales documents. Confirm specifications against the product source before publishing.

tone_examples.tone: Technical, factual and benefit-led. Explain what the product does and where it is used.
Analytical and educational. Explain the industry challenge before connecting it to machine vision.
Direct, informative and action-oriented. State event, location, booth and meeting invitation clearly.
Professional and human, without forcing a sales message.

applications.name: Trade Show Roll-up Banner
applications.description: A vertical, high-visibility format for exhibition spaces.
applications.hierarchy: Brand → short core message → product/application visual → key proof points → contact or QR.
applications.components: Logo, short headline, one dominant visual, up to three proof points, QR/contact details.
applications.template: Design for quick recognition from several meters away; keep copy short and contrast strong.

applications.name: Product One-pager
applications.description: A concise product sheet for sales conversations and event follow-up.
applications.hierarchy: Product name → product image → key benefits → specifications → applications → CTA.
applications.components: Logo, product image, concise feature list, verified technical table, application image and contact CTA.
applications.template: Use a clear grid and consistent specification table; do not invent product specifications.

applications.name: Social Content
applications.description: A repeatable visual system for LinkedIn and other social channels.
applications.hierarchy: One key message → supporting visual → short proof point → brand signature.
applications.components: Logo, headline, image or diagram, restrained supporting shapes and optional CTA.
applications.template: Build reusable Figma components and adapt the same content idea to the platform format.

applications.name: Trade Show Campaign
applications.description: A connected set of pre-show, during-show and post-show communications.
applications.hierarchy: Event identity → stage-specific message → event/product visual → next action.
applications.components: Pre-show announcement, on-site update, post-show recap and shared event information.
applications.template: Keep event name, date, booth and visual identity consistent across all campaign pieces.
